source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Compensation, offsetting a perceived weakness by excelling elsewhere, rather than the entirely unrelated interest the colleague is currently assuming this represents","B":"Projection, attributing one's own feelings to another person, which does not describe this particular pattern of channeling effort into another area","C":"Regression, reverting to an earlier stage of development, which does not describe this particular pattern of excelling in a new area","D":"Denial, refusing to acknowledge an uncomfortable reality, which does not describe this client's active engagement with and effort toward this other pursuit"}}
source_row.rationale: Compensation is a defense mechanism in which a person makes up for a perceived weakness, limitation, or deficiency in one area of life by putting extra effort into and excelling in a different area, partly as a way of offsetting feelings of inadequacy related to the original limitation — generally considered a relatively adaptive defense mechanism when used in moderation.
source_row.source_detail: Recognition of Compensation as a Coping Strategy
source_row.source_name: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing Foundations — Compensation as a Defense Mechanism
source_row.stem: A client who struggles significantly with a particular physical limitation puts intense effort into excelling in a different area, such as academics or a creative pursuit, partly to offset feelings of inadequacy related to the limitation, and a colleague assumes this drive must simply reflect a completely unrelated personal interest with no deeper connection.
